A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and three-stage symbolic mechanism. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original identity-rule task performance, causal interventions, attention analyses, representational similarity analyses, and ablations in Llama3-70B.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical analyses and reports additional model evaluations, analogy experiments, decoding results, and error analyses.

M1.justification: The core symbol-abstraction, symbolic-induction, and retrieval mechanism and causal-patching Algorithm 1 are retained. The new binding discussion and post-retrieval MLP account elaborate the interpretation of existing transformer components; they do not document a redesigned model or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates ABA/ABB identity rules. V2 adds successor/predecessor letter-string analogies and synonym/antonym verbal analogies (Appendix C.5). It also uses length-four rules AABA, ABCB, and ABCC to distinguish representational hypotheses (Appendix B.4), substantially extending task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds random-head ablation alongside the retained control that ablates low-scoring heads in the same layers. Standard induction-head and function-vector comparisons remain, with an additional function-vector variant evaluated at in-context example positions (Table 1).

E3.justification: Reported causal-mediation sampling changes from 20 prompts to 100 per direction, 200 total; ablation sampling changes from 20 to 40 prompts. Figures 3–4 replace top-10 head selection with statistically significant heads. V2 also adds 13-model, 1–10-shot evaluation, task-specific analogy scoring, and token-disjoint probe splits.

E4.justification: V2 adds component-level RSA, a test distinguishing positional from previous-variable representations, position-specific function-vector analyses, random ablation controls, and within/between-task comparisons. Appendix C additionally tests MLP involvement, decoding on unseen tokens, and differences between correct and error trials. These substantially deepen tests of the proposed mechanism.

E5.justification: V2 introduces 5,000-permutation testing with family-wise error control for causal-mediation scores, replacing simple zero-clipping in Figure 2. It adds 95% binomial confidence intervals, standard deviations over 10 random-ablation runs, and significance tests for correlations and error analyses. The original four-seed prefix-matching procedure remains.

E6.justification: The reported two-shot identity-rule accuracy remains 95%, but symbolic-induction correlations change from 0.13 to 0.11 with standard induction scores and from 0.82 to 0.86 with function-vector scores. V2 adds extensive model and analogy results, plus decoding accuracies of 98.63% and 98.10% (Table 6). Revised existing measurements accompany changed analysis settings.

T1.justification: The context constructions and causal-mediation equations retain the same mathematical content. Neither version supplies a theorem or proof that is subsequently revised. The added binding discussion is conceptual, while permutation testing and representational hypotheses support empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated contribution from identifying mechanisms for rule induction in one Llama model to evidence across three reasoning tasks and multiple model families. V2 explicitly claims robust support in Gemma-2, Qwen2.5, and Llama-3.1, while qualifying the evidence for GPT-2.

C2.justification: V1 interprets token information in head outputs as approximate symbolism; v2 argues that invariant variables can nevertheless occupy subspaces. V2 also adds a binding account, separates local function-vector computation from aggregation, discusses scale dependence and task specialization, and proposes post-retrieval MLP transformations for non-identity relations.

D1.justification: V2 specifies bfloat16 loading, model-specific GPU use, patching before the head-output projection, detailed component and position choices, verbal-data generation and filtering, and probe splits. A named planned code/data repository replaces the generic release-on-acceptance promise; the PDF does not establish that release has occurred.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused connections to concept vectors, symbolic circuits in synthetic-task models, external-memory binding, and function-vector development. The central positioning relative to abstractors and emergent symbolic computation remains. Numerous other reference changes update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: The main section order and much existing prose remain. V2 revises the abstract, introduction, and final discussion, clarifies causal-mediation explanations, adds a Binding subsection and Impact Statement, and extends the appendix organization. These are targeted narrative changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 redraws heatmaps, changes color scales and significance displays, and adds random-ablation curves with uncertainty bars. New patching schematics, model comparisons, analogy displays, and seven tables substantially expand the presentation. V1's appendix Figures 6–7 are retained as v2 Figures 10–11.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited validation on one model and one simple task. Broader evaluations, controlled head selection, random ablations, token-disjoint decoding, and error analyses strengthen the central evidence. GPT-2 exceptions and task-specific differences also clarify applicability. Broad necessity claims remain stronger than the tested scope, but the empirical and reproducibility gains substantially improve overall quality.
